Hi Alex —

Great to meet you and the Acme team on today's call. Thanks for walking through the primary RAG use cases (customer self-serve KB + compliance search) — really helpful to hear the typical query characteristics. As promised, summary + next steps below.

Recap (high level):
- Primary objective: authoritative, grounded answers for customer support and compliance teams.
- Query profile: short queries (3-12 tokens) plus longer multi-sentence follow-ups; many queries need source attribution.
- Success metrics: grounding precision, answer correctness, and latency <= 300ms P50 for single-turn queries.

Recommended technical starting point (what we'll prototype in Week 1):
1) Model choice: try Mistral-7B-q4 + Redwood reranker (mid-tier) for an initial cost/performance baseline; for higher accuracy runs test a 13B quantized variant we have in our catalog.
2) Retrieval: dense + sparse hybrid. Use ACME KB snapshots + embeddings with 384-d vector size; initial k=8 retrieval, rerank top 16.
3) Reranker: Redwood-RR-small for latency-sensitive flows, Redwood-RR-large for accuracy-focused flows.
4) Prompt sets & evals: please find attached the prompt set (acme_prompt_set_v3.csv). We'll run the redwood reranker eval and share the report.

Deliverables & timeline:
- Today: this recap + attachments (prompt set).
- By Thu (48 hrs): baseline eval report with 2 model configs + recommended reranker (we'll upload to Drive).
- Next Tue: quick demo of prototype + mutual action plan for Dedicated capacity if the results look good.

Action items for Acme:
- Share one-week query logs (anonymized) or a sample of ~500 queries so we can run embedding/recall analysis.
- Confirm whether legal needs to be looped in now for data residency (CC'd legal in case).

Attachments: acme_prompt_set_v3.csv (prompt examples & expected labels)

Happy to hop on a 20-min technical sync with Rishi and David if you want to deep-dive retrieval settings.

Hey Alex — quick technical notes to address your questions and to document what we'll prototype: 

Latency vs precision (rerankers):
- Redwood-RR-small: median rerank latency ~30-40ms on our dedicated infra (quantized weights), precision@1 ~0.72 on similar KB tasks. Good default for interactive support where P50 latency matters.
- Redwood-RR-large: median rerank latency ~90-120ms, precision@1 ~0.82. Use for compliance flows or canned reports where accuracy is paramount.

Retrieval integration:
- No need to rip out Elasticsearch. We typically augment BM25 + existing ES pipeline by adding dense embeddings as an additional retrieval pass and then merging candidates (hybrid merge). For a low-effort eval we can run a shadow pipeline that queries the vector store in parallel and returns combined candidate set.

Proposed eval config (we'll run these and include results in the report):
- Config A (latency-first): Mistral-7B-q4 + Redwood-RR-small, k_retrieve=8, rerank_top=16, vector dim=384, chunking at ~750 tokens.
- Config B (accuracy-first): 13B-quantized + Redwood-RR-large, k_retrieve=12, rerank_top=32, chunking at ~1024 tokens.

Grounding metrics we'll measure: grounding precision (source precision@1/3), hallucination rate (contradictory assertions against KB), and attribution coverage (percentage of answers with at least one cited source). We'll include confidence thresholds to tune recall/precision.

Attachments: I'm attaching the initial reranker eval (redwood_reranker_eval_report.pdf) with preliminary results from a similar enterprise KB. Also including a simple architecture diagram (acme_MVP_map.png).
